title: Tensor and Hom of a DG bimodule on homotopy categories
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups; triangles are the distinguished mapping-cone triangles. For right DG modules $X,Y$ write $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(X,Y)^r$ for degree-$r$ graded right $A$-linear maps, with differential $df=d_Yf-(-1)^rfd_X$. Write $K(A,d)$ for DG modules with morphisms $H^0\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(X,Y)$; its localization functor is $Q_A:K(A,d)\to D(A,d)$. Let $(B,d)$ be another DG algebra over $\mathbf Z$ and $N$ a DG $(A,B)$-bimodule: its unital left and right graded actions commute and satisfy $d(an)=d(a)n+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(n)$ and $d(nb)=d(n)b+(-1)^{|n|}n\,d(b)$. For a right DG $A$-module $M$ put $F_NM=M\otimes_A N$, the quotient of the graded tensor over $\mathbf Z$ by $ma\otimes n=m\otimes an$, with $d(m\otimes n)=dm\otimes n+(-1)^{|m|}m\otimes dn$. For a right DG $B$-module $Y$ put $G_NY=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(N,Y)$ with right $A$-action $(fa)(n)=f(an)$. These constructions induce exact functors [def-weil-triangulated-category] $F_N:K(A,d)\to K(B,d)$ and $G_N:K(B,d)\to K(A,d)$, for the mapping-cone triangulated structures: the shift below, and as distinguished triangles those isomorphic to $U\xrightarrow{u}V\xrightarrow{i}C(u)\xrightarrow{-p}U[1]$ for degree-zero chain maps $u$, where $C(u)^i=V^i\oplus U^{i+1}$ with $d(v,x)=(dv+u(x),-dx)$ and componentwise right action, $i(v)=(v,0)$ and $p(v,x)=x$. Currying defines an isomorphism of complexes of abelian groups, natural in $M,Y$, $$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(F_NM,Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(M,G_NY),\qquad g\longmapsto(m\longmapsto(n\longmapsto g(m\otimes n))).$$ Its inverse evaluates $f$ at $m,n$. Use the shift $X[k]^i=X^{i+k}$ with differential $(-1)^kd_X$ and unchanged right graded action. The shift comparisons $F_N(M[k])\cong(F_NM)[k]$ and $G_N(Y[k])\cong(G_NY)[k]$ are the identity on the underlying elements and graded maps. The induced $H^0$ currying bijection is compatible with simultaneous shifts of $M$ and $Y$ under these comparisons. No quasi-isomorphism preservation or derived-functor assertion is included.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dg-homotopy-acyclic-localization] separately to $A$ and $B$. Its triangulation clause gives exactly the homotopy categories and shifts in the statement. We use its cone convention $C(u)^i=V^i\oplus U^{i+1}$, $d(v,x)=(d_Vv+u(x),-d_Ux)$ for $u:U\to V$, with cone triangle $U\to V\to C(u)\xrightarrow{-p}U[1]$. Its assertions about acyclics and localization are not needed here. In the calculations below write $\delta h=d h-(-1)^{|h|}h d$ for a Hom differential.

source.place: Tag 09KJ, proposition-homotopy-category-triangulated; cone convention as in Tag 09KF, lemma-the-same-up-to-isomorphisms.

proof.text:
The tensor differential is well defined on the stated quotient. For $|m|=p$, $|a|=s$, its values on $ma\otimes n$ and $m\otimes an$ both reduce to
$$dm\otimes an+(-1)^p m\otimes da\,n+(-1)^{p+s}m\otimes a\,dn.$$
The right $B$-action is $(m\otimes n)b=m\otimes nb$; commuting actions on $N$ preserve the balancing relations. Expanding twice gives $d^2(m\otimes n)=d^2m\otimes n+((-1)^{p+1}+(-1)^p)dm\otimes dn+m\otimes d^2n=0$. Expanding $d(m\otimes nb)$ gives $d(m\otimes n)b+(-1)^{p+|n|}(m\otimes n)db$. Thus this is a right DG $B$-module.

source.place: Tag 09LM, lemma-tensor, preceding construction in section-bimodules-tensor.

proof.text:
For $f:N\to Y$ of degree $r$, $\delta f$ is right $B$-linear: expansion at $nb$ cancels the two terms $(-1)^{r+|n|}f(n)db$. Moreover $\delta^2 f=d_Y^2f-fd_N^2=0$. Precomposition gives $(fa)b=f(ab)$ for $a,b\in A$, and $(fa)(nb)=f(an)b$ for $b\in B$, so it defines the stated graded right $A$-action. For $|a|=s$ the differential identity is
$$(\delta(fa))(n)=d_Yf(an)-(-1)^{r+s}f(a\,dn)=((\delta f)a+(-1)^r f\,da)(n),$$
where the last equality expands $d_N(an)=da\,n+(-1)^s a\,dn$. This verifies the right DG $A$-module Leibniz rule, with no sign in the action itself.

source.place: Tag 0FQQ, lemma-hom, preceding construction in section-bimodules-hom.

proof.text:
On any homogeneous right $A$-linear map $h:M\to M'$ of degree $r$, set $F_N(h)(m\otimes n)=h(m)\otimes n$. Balancing follows from $h(ma)=h(m)a$. On a homogeneous $m$ of degree $p$ one has
$$\delta(F_Nh)(m\otimes n)=d_{M'}h(m)\otimes n+(-1)^{p+r}h(m)\otimes dn-(-1)^rh(dm)\otimes n-(-1)^{p+r}h(m)\otimes dn=F_N(\delta h)(m\otimes n).$$
Identities, composition and addition are preserved on every generator $m\otimes n$. Hence $F_N$ acts by chain maps on all Hom complexes.

For a homogeneous right $B$-linear map $h:Y\to Y'$ of degree $r$, set $G_N(h)(f)=h\circ f$. This is $A$-linear since $(h\circ(fa))(n)=h(f(an))$. For $|f|=q$, expansion gives
$$\delta(G_Nh)(f)=d_{Y'}hf-(-1)^{r+q}hf d_N-(-1)^rh(d_Yf-(-1)^q f d_N)=(\delta h)f.$$
Again identities, composition and addition are preserved. Both constructions therefore send closed degree-zero maps to such maps and boundaries $\delta h$, $|h|=-1$, to boundaries. Thus $[u]\mapsto[F_Nu]$ and $[v]\mapsto[G_Nv]$ are well-defined additive functors on the respective $H^0$ homotopy categories.

source.place: Tag 0FQQ, lemma-hom, proof; Tag 09LM, lemma-tensor, last assertion.

proof.text: For a degree-$r$ map $g:F_NM\to Y$ define $\Phi(g)(m)(n)=g(m\otimes n)$. For $|m|=p$, $\Phi(g)(m)$ has degree $p+r$. It is $B$-linear because $g$ is, and $\Phi(g)(ma)(n)=g(ma\otimes n)=g(m\otimes an)=(\Phi(g)(m)a)(n)$, giving $A$-linearity. Conversely $f\mapsto((m,n)\mapsto f(m)(n))$ is additive in each variable and balanced since $f(ma)(n)=f(m)(an)$; it therefore extends uniquely from the generators of the tensor quotient to a degree-$r$ $B$-linear map $\Psi(f)$. Evaluation gives $\Psi\Phi(g)(m\otimes n)=g(m\otimes n)$ and $\Phi\Psi(f)(m)(n)=f(m)(n)$. These formulas give inverse additive maps in every degree, without any boundedness assumption: an element of the tensor has finite support, whereas a homogeneous Hom map is an unrestricted family over the source degrees.

source.place: Tag 09LN, lemma-tensor-hom-adjunction, omitted proof and bilinear-map hint, expanded explicitly.

proof.text:
For $|g|=r$ and $|m|=p$, expanding either differential gives exactly
$$(\delta\Phi(g))(m)(n)=d_Yg(m\otimes n)-(-1)^{p+r}g(m\otimes dn)-(-1)^rg(dm\otimes n)=\Phi(\delta g)(m)(n).$$
Thus $\Phi$ and its inverse are isomorphisms of complexes. For degree-zero chain maps $u:M'\to M$ and $v:Y\to Y'$, both sides of the naturality square send $g$ to the family $(m',n)\mapsto v(g(u(m')\otimes n))$. This proves naturality in both variables. The inverse chain maps restrict to inverse maps on degree-zero kernels and degree-zero boundaries, hence induce the claimed natural $H^0$ bijection.

source.place: Tag 09LN, lemma-tensor-hom-adjunction, differential-graded assertion and proof hint.

proof.text:
The tensor shift comparison sends $m\otimes n$ to the same tensor. If $m$ has original degree $p$, the differential in $F_N(M[k])$ is $(-1)^kdm\otimes n+(-1)^{p-k}m\otimes dn$, which equals $(-1)^k d_{F_NM}(m\otimes n)$ since $p-k$ and $p+k$ have the same parity. For a degree-$r$ element $f$ of $G_N(Y[k])$, its original degree as a map to $Y$ is $r+k$, and
$$\delta_{G_N(Y[k])}f=(-1)^kd_Yf-(-1)^rf d_N=(-1)^k(d_Yf-(-1)^{r+k}f d_N).$$
These are precisely the shifted differentials on the other sides. The identity comparisons respect the unchanged right actions and are inverse degreewise; on morphisms their naturality follows by evaluating $h(m)\otimes n$ and $h\circ f$. They are compatible with iterated shifts because their underlying maps are identities.

For a chain map $u:U\to V$ of right DG $A$-modules the map
$$F_NC(u)\longrightarrow C(F_Nu),\qquad (v,x)\otimes n\longmapsto(v\otimes n,x\otimes n)$$
is a graded $B$-linear isomorphism. Its inverse sends $(v\otimes n,0)$ to $(v,0)\otimes n$ and $(0,x\otimes n)$ to $(0,x)\otimes n$, extending additively; the balancing relations make these assignments well defined. For $(v,x)\in C(u)^p$, both differentials under this comparison give
$$(dv\otimes n+u(x)\otimes n+(-1)^pv\otimes dn,\ -dx\otimes n+(-1)^px\otimes dn).$$
The second sign uses $|x|=p+1$. The comparison intertwines inclusion and projection and uses exactly the shift comparison of the preceding step on $U[1]$.

source.place: Tag 09LR, lemma-bc-homotopy, with the cone computation underlying lemma-functor-between-ABC written out.

proof.text:
For a chain map $u:U\to V$ of right DG $B$-modules, projecting to the two coordinates gives a graded $A$-linear isomorphism $G_NC(u)\to C(G_Nu)$. A degree-$r$ map into $C(u)$ has components $(a,b)$ where $|a|=r$ and $|b|=r+1$, and its differential has components
$$(\delta a+u b,\ -\delta b),$$
by expanding $d_{C(u)}(a,b)-(-1)^r(a,b)d_N$. Conversely $(a,b)$ defines the map $n\mapsto(a(n),b(n))$, so no preservation of infinite sums or products is required. This comparison also intertwines inclusion and projection, with the shift comparison of step 8. Consequently both functors carry the cone triangles specified in step 1, including their third arrows $-p$, to cone triangles. Every distinguished triangle is isomorphic to one of these by [lem-sfb-dg-homotopy-acyclic-localization]; a functor takes an isomorphism and its inverse to inverse maps. Thus both additive, shift-compatible functors preserve distinguished triangles and are exact.

source.place: Tag 09LH, lemma-restriction-homotopy; Tag 09LR, lemma-bc-homotopy; their cone argument from lemma-functor-between-ABC.

proof.text: Finally, a closed degree-zero $g:F_NM\to Y$ shifted simultaneously in source and target represents $g[k]:F_N(M[k])\to Y[k]$ by the same underlying rule, using step 8. Its curry sends $(m,n)$ to $g(m\otimes n)$, which is also the rule for $\Phi(g)[k]:M[k]\to(G_NY)[k]\cong G_N(Y[k])$. Thus the shift square agrees already on closed representatives. If $g-g'=\delta h$ with $|h|=-1$, then after simultaneous shift $g[k]-g'[k]=\delta((-1)^kh[k])$, since both source and target differentials acquired $(-1)^k$. The chain isomorphism of step 7 carries this boundary to the corresponding boundary on the curried side. Hence the square is well defined and commutes on $H^0$ classes, proving the last compatibility clause.
